title: BGP-specific gate/sub-gate guidance
note: Project-specific companion explanations ('For BGP') for the institutional gate/sub-gate catalogue, keyed by the same track/gate/item reference the generic item_guidance uses. Explanatory only -- not evidence, does not itself satisfy or approve any gate. G4-R.01-10 map onto this project's combined G4.01-10; G4.01-11 (source document numbering) map onto G4.11-21; G4-R.11 (recommendation-issued) has no separate item in this combined-G4 tracker edition and is intentionally omitted.

items.Gate 1.01: Describe BGP's scattered-evidence problem, intended small-agency and consultancy users, proposed outcome and project owner in its intake record.
items.Gate 1.02: Attach examples of difficulty finding approvals, inconsistent tracker records or user interviews; distinguish observations from assumptions about demand.
items.Gate 1.03: Identify BGP contributors, client approvers, sponsors, administrators and assurance reviewers, and the value each expects.
items.Gate 1.04: State the desired outcome as reliable, retrievable governance decisions and simpler user journeys, not merely building a web application.
items.Gate 1.05: Record initial concerns about cross-tenant disclosure, false approval, audit tampering, personal data and licensed starter content.
items.Gate 1.06: Explain why turning the single-organisation tracker into a multi-tenant product is project work, and estimate the discovery effort without inventing a deadline.
items.Gate 1.07: Check available BGP development and independent-review capacity against other commitments before promising delivery dates.
items.Gate 1.08: Record BGP's Project Class A and Software Class 3 assessment and any later approved reclassification; do not reduce them because the first prototype is small.
items.Gate 1.09: Record whether BGP discovery should proceed and why the expected governance value justifies that investigation.
items.Gate 1.10: Link the actual BGP intake decision and its authority; do not use this guide as a substitute for that decision.
items.Gate 1.11: If BGP used an expedited intake path, link its specific authority and limits. Development-initiation approval alone is not an expedited spending authorisation.
items.Gate 2.01: Use BGP's charter to define the multi-tenant governance product, its owner, intended outcomes, exclusions and governing approvals.
items.Gate 2.02: Explain BGP's expected adoption, operating costs and value to agencies or consultancies; identify uncertain commercial assumptions rather than invent revenue figures.
items.Gate 2.03: Assess whether the team can deliver tenant isolation, protected decisions, reliable recovery and accessible workflows within available resources.
items.Gate 2.04: Compare retaining the tracker, adapting an existing tool and building BGP; explain why configurable governance and trustworthy records justify the chosen approach.
items.Gate 2.05: Use Blueprint Section 2 and frontend Section 20 to distinguish mandatory governance workflows from excluded scheduling, resource planning and issue tracking.
items.Gate 2.06: Prepare BGP estimates by WP01–WP14, including assurance, usability testing and operations; record ranges and staffing assumptions under DEC09.
items.Gate 2.07: Start BGP risks for tenant isolation, decision durability, rule complexity, licensing, operator access and independent-review availability.
items.Gate 2.08: Resolve named delivery and independent-review appointments under DEC01; Freston Kenny Adedeme's document ownership does not automatically fill every delivery role.
items.Gate 2.09: Record the Class A/Class 3 alignment and show how BGP's project decisions reuse engineering evidence without duplicating approval work.
items.Gate 2.10: State BGP's actual approval roles, Class A reporting and tolerances, change authority and separation of duties; do not infer authority from a username.
items.Gate 2.11: Plan BGP adoption and outcome measures, name the operational benefits owner and reserve the interim three-month and formal six-month reviews.
items.Gate 2.12: Link BGP's actual charter/project-authorisation decision. APR-001 and FE-APR-001 approve development baselines, not every governing gate.
items.Gate 3.01: Baseline REQ-001–REQ-058 and FE-001–FE-102 with their conditional scope, test links and explicit exclusions; retain their original IDs.
items.Gate 3.02: Use WP01–WP14 as BGP's work breakdown, assigning implementation and review work rather than treating a document approval as completed code.
items.Gate 3.03: Schedule package dependencies, decision deadlines, independent testing and recovery rehearsals; include capacity and contingency under DEC09.
items.Gate 3.04: Record BGP staffing, environments, tools, assurance funding and operating resources with actual authorised values, not assumed budgets.
items.Gate 3.05: Assign delivery, technical, UX, QA, security/privacy, data, service and release responsibilities; retain explicit vacancies until appointments are accepted.
items.Gate 3.06: Plan TST-001–TST-058, AC01–AC23 and all applicable frontend checks, including independent security and inclusive usability evidence.
items.Gate 3.07: Maintain BGP's risk register with response owners for isolation, stale decisions, tampering, recovery, template escalation and misunderstood approval.
items.Gate 3.08: Set BGP's Class A review calendar and define what the sponsor, contributors, reviewers and operations team receive.
items.Gate 3.09: Plan BGP membership checks, MFA, RLS, key custody, audit protection, backups, export controls and incident response under REQ-001–009 and REQ-026–029.
items.Gate 3.10: Define how BGP requirement changes, ADRs, schema migrations, code reviews, template versions and decision corrections are controlled.
items.Gate 3.11: Plan BGP onboarding, operating handover, migration, rollback, support instructions and project closure without implying service retirement.
items.Gate 3.12: Include the protected benefits-review effort and independent assurance in BGP's authorised plan; retain the three-month and six-month review points.
items.Gate 3.13: Check that BGP's requirements, package dependencies, API contracts, delivery estimates and acceptance plan agree and are feasible together.
items.Gate 3.14: Show that BGP's release author cannot be its sole release approver; record required independent assurance and any permitted compensating arrangement.
items.Gate 3.15: Complete the plan-readiness review using BGP's actual baseline versions, assigned people, decisions and evidence links.
items.Gate 3.16: Link the authorised BGP delivery-readiness decision and its conditions to the approved integrated plan and G2 design evidence.
items.Gate 4.01: Record a BGP kickoff confirming the product boundaries, synthetic-data restriction, responsibilities, review process and evidence expectations.
items.Gate 4.02: Authorise BGP work packages with defined outputs and test evidence, using the blueprint dependencies and actual assigned owners.
items.Gate 4.03: Keep BGP's requirement ledger, decisions, risks, code references and acceptance evidence in controlled locations with stable links.
items.Gate 4.04: Review BGP journeys and controls incrementally, especially isolation and approval semantics, before the final release review.
items.Gate 4.05: Track any BGP hosting, testing, licensing or other external obligations against recorded approvals; do not treat an unselected supplier as contracted.
items.Gate 4.06: Prepare BGP user guidance, support procedures, migration rehearsal and release environment alongside feature development.
items.Gate 4.07: For each delivered BGP package, link the implementation revision, passing checks, reviewer and accepted limitations; a closed task label alone is insufficient.
items.Gate 4.08: Identify the BGP commit/build, environment, synthetic fixtures and actual test results in every acceptance report.
items.Gate 4.09: Show the release's defect and residual-risk position, including no open S1 and authorised treatment of any S2.
items.Gate 4.10: Demonstrate that BGP users can complete the core journeys and the service owner can monitor, support and recover the release.
items.Gate 4.11: Link BGP's isolation tests, privacy review, penetration-test findings where required, secrets checks and approved residual-risk decisions.
items.Gate 4.12: Link BGP's named acceptance authority, Class A Project Authority concurrence and engineering release authorisation for the exact deliverable.
items.Gate 5.01: Maintain BGP's Class A weekly delivery review, at least fortnightly formal status and the directive's monthly continuation review, plus triggered reviews.
items.Gate 5.02: Report BGP package progress, blocked decisions, frontend/backend integration, assurance readiness, costs, forecasts and decisions required.
items.Gate 5.03: Base BGP's status on linked implementation and review evidence, not the number of documents approved or tasks marked closed.
items.Gate 5.04: Compare BGP forecasts with the approved Class A cost and schedule tolerances and its quality/risk boundaries; do not invent a baseline where none is recorded.
items.Gate 5.05: Explain BGP delays or cost changes in terms of causes such as unresolved durability choices, contract gaps or independent-review capacity.
items.Gate 5.06: Record triggers such as a failed isolation check, uncertain recovery guarantee, missing assurance, scope expansion or a forecast tolerance breach.
items.Gate 5.07: Record when each BGP material trigger was detected and when the required review took place, applying the governing two/five-business-day limits.
items.Gate 5.08: Track BGP corrective actions through implementation and retest, retaining the evidence that the action addressed the original problem.
items.Gate 5.09: Retain BGP's original commitments, approved changes and current forecast when approving a revised baseline.
items.Gate 5.10: Record the actual BGP continuation, correction, rebaseline or stop decision for each occurrence; keep earlier occurrences intact.
items.Gate 6.01: Obtain BGP acceptance against the applicable REQ, FE, TST and AC baseline, identifying the accepted release and limitations.
items.Gate 6.02: Complete BGP release, support, training, security, backup and tested recovery handover for the accepted service.
items.Gate 6.03: Transfer BGP code, environments, data responsibilities, licences, runbooks, monitoring and outstanding actions to named receiving owners.
items.Gate 6.04: Settle or transfer BGP project contracts, invoices, equipment and accounts; remove development access that is no longer needed.
items.Gate 6.05: Record BGP's final delivery cost, schedule, scope and quality against its authorised commitments.
items.Gate 6.06: Archive BGP's approved baselines, release evidence, immutable decisions, review records, lessons and closure report under the retention policy.
items.Gate 6.07: Record how BGP developers and reviewers are released or reassigned while the ongoing service remains adequately staffed.
items.Gate 6.08: Assign BGP adoption/outcome measurement and outstanding corrective actions to their post-project owners.
items.Gate 6.09: Apply the approved retention/legal-hold decisions to BGP records; do not destroy attribution or evidence merely because development has ended.
items.Gate 6.10: Set BGP's project record to Operational - Benefits Pending when appropriate, with the formal Gate 7 date and evidence owner.
items.Gate 6.11: Prepare BGP's closure report covering acceptance, handover, final performance, unresolved actions and benefits-review arrangements.
items.Gate 6.12: Link the sponsor's BGP closure decision; keep service operations and the later benefits review separate from project delivery closure.
items.Gate 7.01: Define BGP benefits using measured baselines and approved targets; possible measures include evidence-retrieval time, adoption and unaided task completion.
items.Gate 7.02: Record the Class A protected review effort used for BGP's benefits evaluation rather than absorbing it into untracked support work.
items.Gate 7.03: Collect BGP usage evidence by intended role and organisation type without treating raw sign-up counts as successful adoption.
items.Gate 7.04: Compare BGP's actual governance outcomes with its approved benefits targets, keeping usability acceptance results distinct from long-term business benefits.
items.Gate 7.05: Record whether BGP introduced extra administration, support burden, cost or confusion for contributors and client approvers.
items.Gate 7.06: Review assumptions about agency demand, template flexibility, onboarding difficulty and the effort needed to maintain trustworthy records.
items.Gate 7.07: Assign BGP improvements, follow-on investment or retirement proposals to named owners with recorded authority.
items.Gate 7.08: Feed BGP lessons into its product backlog, training and future delivery practice; institutional policy changes need their own approval.
items.Gate 7.09: Change BGP's project status to Closed - Benefits Reviewed only after the benefits evidence and decision are recorded.
items.Gate 7.10: Link the sponsor's BGP benefits decision, including whether to sustain, improve, expand, replace or retire the outcome.
items.G0.01: Use BGP's concept/intake record to explain configurable frameworks, evidence, decisions, audit history and intended users.
items.G0.02: Assess the feasibility of BGP's FastAPI/PostgreSQL direction, multi-tenant controls, decision integrity, recovery and accessible interface.
items.G0.03: Record BGP's named sponsor, delivery lead and technical owner, referring to DEC01 for unresolved appointments.
items.G0.04: Describe BGP's initial first-release scope, stakeholders, Software Class 3 assessment and project-specific risks.
items.G0.05: Record why a hosted governance platform is preferred over extending the local tracker or using an existing product.
items.G0.06: Link the actual authority and time/resource limits for BGP discovery or local prototypes, including the synthetic-data boundary.
items.G0.07: Keep BGP's G0 record linked to its intake evidence and actual authority, separately from the guide itself.
items.G0.08: Check that BGP's intended outcome, responsible owner, data restrictions and acceptance authority were established before relying on development commitment.
items.G1.01: Use the approved Blueprint v0.2 requirement catalogue and Frontend Requirements v1.1 as BGP's linked controlled requirements set.
items.G1.02: Describe BGP registration, memberships, template versions, project creation, evidence revisions, decisions, exceptions, history and export/import rules.
items.G1.03: Record BGP's availability, recovery, decision-loss, accessibility and usability requirements; resolve unspecified numeric budgets through DEC08.
items.G1.04: Use UI01–UI10 and journeys A–E to cover sign-in, first project, assigned evidence, decision review/correction and framework authoring.
items.G1.05: Link each BGP REQ to its TST, relevant directive AC and applicable FE checks; all expected results remain planned until executed.
items.G1.06: Inventory BGP identity, membership, project, evidence, audit, decision and optional attachment data with sensitivity and handling rules.
items.G1.07: State BGP's MFA, tenant isolation, separation, encryption, operator-access and attribution requirements with their identified risks.
items.G1.08: Maintain a BGP ledger linking REQ/FE to WP, implementation, test, evidence and reviewer while preserving existing identifiers.
items.G1.09: Record review and baseline versions for BGP's approved requirements; retain APR-001 and FE-APR-001 within their document-approval scope.
items.G1.10: Check BGP requirements for ambiguous approval meaning, missing API details, conflicting retention rules and untestable performance claims.
items.G1.11: Track missing BGP choices under DEC01–DEC12 and frontend API gaps; link later resolutions instead of assuming old gaps remain open.
items.G1.12: Link the actual BGP G1 requirements-baseline approval and any conditions; a frontend supplement does not waive system review.
items.G2.01: Update BGP's package plan and estimates using the approved requirements and actual decisions, not assumed staffing or completion dates.
items.G2.02: Show BGP's separately planned independent QA, penetration testing, accessibility/usability checks and recovery assurance effort.
items.G2.03: Document BGP's browser, same-origin API, modular service, PostgreSQL store, workers and any enabled object storage, including data flows.
items.G2.04: Record BGP architecture choices for sessions, frontend stack, durability, rule limits, key custody, retention and import with reasons and rejected alternatives.
items.G2.05: Provide BGP UI01–UI10 designs, tenant-scoped database relationships and complete API schemas, including the gaps listed in frontend Section 16.
items.G2.06: Model BGP threats such as tenant leakage, role escalation, stale approvals, evidence substitution, privileged tampering and unsafe imports.
items.G2.07: Design BGP session/MFA checks, least-privilege database access, CSRF where applicable, secret storage, encryption and independent verification custody.
items.G2.08: Plan BGP's two-tenant tests, migration/rollback, monitoring, support, one-hour ordinary-data RPO and eight-hour restoration target.
items.G2.09: Use controlled BGP prototypes to prove uncertain RLS, rule-interpreter, decision-concurrency and durability designs with synthetic fixtures.
items.G2.10: Review whether BGP modules enforce clear responsibilities, tenant boundaries, observable failures and recoverability without relying on frontend trust.
items.G2.11: Link BGP's G2 design approval to the actual ADRs and required security review, showing which DEC choices are resolved or still blocking affected work.
items.G3.01: Identify BGP's controlled frontend/API source, migrations, worker code, infrastructure definitions and release configuration.
items.G3.02: Link BGP changes to their REQ/FE/WP records and reviewed commits or pull requests.
items.G3.03: Provide BGP branch-protection evidence showing that review and required CI checks cannot be skipped through the normal merge path.
items.G3.04: Record competent independent review of BGP's tenant, approval, data and infrastructure changes at the required risk depth.
items.G3.05: Provide BGP unit and interface tests for rule interpretation, evidence validation, membership, concurrency and client/API state handling.
items.G3.06: Run BGP's build, tests, secret/dependency checks and blocking cross-tenant suite; demonstrate that a planted isolation defect is detected.
items.G3.07: Retain BGP pipeline outputs with exact source revision, configuration and environment so reviewers can reproduce the result.
items.G3.08: Keep BGP's dependency and licence inventory, including frontend packages and the licensing position of any shipped starter content.
items.G3.09: Verify that BGP fixtures, logs, code, bundles and collaboration records contain no live secrets and that approved secret storage is used.
items.G3.10: Record human understanding, review and tests for AI-assisted BGP code; generated output is not automatically accepted.
items.G3.11: Update BGP's API schemas, data model, setup instructions, runbooks and user guidance alongside affected code.
items.G3.12: Maintain BGP's defects, technical debt and deviations; link TR01–TR07 to current evidence without reopening or closing findings merely from this guide.
items.G3.13: Link BGP's G3 decision for the exact candidate build. Code complete permits the relevant testing step, not production deployment.
items.G4.01: Use a BGP risk-based plan covering REQ-001–058, AC01–23, FE-001–102 as applicable, and requirement-specific negative scenarios.
items.G4.02: Record BGP test IDs, steps, expected/actual results, source revision, environment, fixtures and tester/reviewer.
items.G4.03: Run BGP unit, integration, system, regression and user-acceptance checks, including all five essential journeys.
items.G4.04: Test BGP isolation, penetration resistance, decision concurrency, integrity, recovery, portability, accessibility and inclusive task completion.
items.G4.05: Use production-like BGP configurations with fictional tenants and permitted test data; do not copy real customer evidence into uncontrolled tests.
items.G4.06: Maintain BGP's severity-ranked defect list, including approval misunderstanding and cross-tenant disclosure as material release concerns.
items.G4.07: Retest BGP corrections against their original failure and related regression scenarios; link review-closure records to actual supporting results.
items.G4.08: Show that the BGP candidate has no open S1 and that any released S2 has the required residual-risk acceptance.
items.G4.09: Attach BGP security/privacy review and scan reports, including independent penetration testing before general availability.
items.G4.10: Obtain authorised BGP acceptance of core journeys and approved usability targets, including twenty-minute onboarding and 90% unaided completion per group.
items.G4.11: Assemble the BGP release manifest with build ID, approved changes, dependencies, configuration, migrations and known limitations.
items.G4.12: Publish BGP release notes tied to an immutable build and the exact frontend/API versions being deployed.
items.G4.13: Confirm BGP production membership/access controls, infrastructure, monitoring, backup, on-call support and user communications are ready.
items.G4.14: Approve BGP deployment, schema/data migration and rollback plans with explicit go/no-go and rollback authority.
items.G4.15: Separate BGP build credentials from deployment credentials and make the deployment repeatable through controlled procedures or automation.
items.G4.16: Take the required BGP backups/checkpoints and validate recovery before irreversible migration, including decision/manifest reconciliation.
items.G4.17: Hand over BGP operational instructions for alerts, failed saves, pending decisions, integrity incidents, exports and recovery.
items.G4.18: Complete the BGP release-readiness checklist with all applicable system and frontend evidence, not a screenshot-only sign-off.
items.G4.19: Record the named BGP release authority and demonstrate that the sole author is not the sole approver for this Class 3 release.
items.G4.20: After authorisation, deploy BGP and record smoke tests, business checks, health monitoring, deviations and any rollback.
items.G4.21: Record BGP's production-release authorisation before production change, tied to the exact candidate and permitted conditions.
items.G5.01: Register the BGP service, named owner, support contacts and responsibilities for tenancy, integrity and recovery.
items.G5.02: Review BGP deployment and early-life evidence, including successful core journeys and any outstanding service issues.
items.G5.03: Monitor BGP availability, latency, errors, queues, draft-save failures, pending decisions, denied approvals, integrity checks, backups and dependencies.
items.G5.04: Publish BGP support hours, incident contacts, escalation paths and response targets with named responsibility.
items.G5.05: Keep BGP incident, problem, change, maintenance and vulnerability records with owners and dates.
items.G5.06: Investigate significant or recurring BGP failures such as unconfirmed decisions, repeated save loss or integrity mismatches and verify corrective action.
items.G5.07: Track BGP Class 3 critical vulnerability remediation within seven calendar days and high vulnerabilities within thirty, subject to stricter obligations.
items.G5.08: Demonstrate BGP's S1 acknowledgement process meets the one-hour Class 3 target and assigns active ownership.
items.G5.09: Test BGP restoration at least quarterly in a clean environment; check ordinary data against one-hour RPO/eight-hour RTO and acknowledged decisions against the separate zero-loss requirement.
items.G5.10: Review BGP access at least quarterly, including approvers, administrators, service accounts, operators and independent verification custody.
items.G5.11: Apply BGP requirements, review, testing and release controls to later enhancements; do not weaken immutable-history or tenant protections during maintenance.
items.G5.12: Review BGP operational results and maintain improvements linked to user difficulty, support incidents and service measures.
items.G5.13: Record the service and product owners' actual BGP operational acceptance, including any permitted remaining conditions.
items.G6.01: If BGP is being retired, approve the reason, tenant impact, replacement/export arrangements, dependencies and retirement date.
items.G6.02: Plan BGP tenant communication, authorised exports, migrations and reconciliation before any service shutdown.
items.G6.03: Apply BGP's approved retention, legal-hold, actor-attribution and disposal decisions; retain DEC06 resolutions as the policy basis.
items.G6.04: Disable only BGP accounts, integrations, domains, certificates, pipelines and infrastructure included in the approved retirement scope.
items.G6.05: Archive BGP source/releases, configuration, decision records, tests, licences, ADRs and operational evidence under controlled access.
items.G6.06: Record BGP's final asset inventory and the locations and custodians of retained tenant and project records.
items.G6.07: Settle or transfer BGP contractual and financial obligations, including ongoing support commitments if the service continues.
items.G6.08: Document BGP delivery lessons, measured benefits and outstanding actions; preserve links to the later Gate 7 review where still due.
items.G6.09: Obtain the authorised BGP client/sponsor acceptance of the specific closure or retirement scope.
items.G6.10: Record BGP's G6 decision, responsible authorities and evidence; distinguish closing delivery from ending the live platform.
